aiPrompts.script:
Add trckable analytics to this project (the site example.com).

The one thing to add, exactly as written (site id tkb_a1b2c3d4, server https://stats.example.com):

<script
  defer
  data-site="tkb_a1b2c3d4"
  data-domain="example.com"
  src="https://stats.example.com/js/tkb_a1b2c3d4.js">
</script>

Where it goes, depending on the stack:
- Plain HTML, Hugo, Jekyll, Eleventy, Astro, SvelteKit, Angular, Laravel, Rails, Django: inside <head> of the layout every page uses.
- Next.js (App Router): run `npm i trckable`, then in app/layout.tsx add `import { Analytics } from 'trckable/next'` and render `<Analytics site="tkb_a1b2c3d4" host="https://stats.example.com" />` inside <body>. That is enough to start counting. Only if I ask for counting behind ad blockers too: add app/api/e/route.ts with `export { POST } from 'trckable/next'`, set TRCKABLE_HOST=https://stats.example.com and TRCKABLE_PROXY_KEY in .env (ask me for the key; never commit it), and remove host from <Analytics>.
- React, Vite, Vue, Svelte, any bundled app: run `npm i trckable`, then once at startup `import { init } from 'trckable'` and `init({ site: 'tkb_a1b2c3d4', host: 'https://stats.example.com' })`. Use this instead of the script tag, not as well.
- WordPress: add the script tag through a header-scripts plugin (WPCode) or the child theme's wp_head hook, not header.php of a theme that updates.
- I picked "Script tag" in the dashboard: In the <head> of every page.

Rules:
- Add it once. Search the project first for "trckable", "data-site" and "tkb_a1b2c3d4"; if it is already there, fix that one instead of adding a second.
- Keep data-site="tkb_a1b2c3d4" and data-domain="example.com" exactly: the id is how visits reach this site.
- Change nothing else: no other analytics removed, no formatting of unrelated files.

When done: tell me which file you changed, deploy or run the site, open example.com once in a browser, and check https://stats.example.com/example.com — the first visit shows up there within seconds.
